title: Advice polynomial time for all-ones sublanguages
statement: Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet such that every word in $L$ consists entirely of $1$s. Then $L$ belongs to polynomial time with polynomial-length advice: there are natural numbers $c,C,d$, an advice string of length exactly $C(n+1)^d$ for each input length $n$, and a finite Turing machine that decides membership in $L$ on input paired with its length-$|x|$ advice within $c(|x|^c+1)$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: Every word in $L$ consists entirely of $1$s
